message.content:
Here’s a mix of classics, cult favorites, recent hits, and hidden gems—so whether you’re into jump‑scares, psychological dread, or cosmic terror, there’s something on this list for you:

| # | Title & Year | Subgenre / Tone | Why It Stands Out |
|---|--------------|-----------------|--------------------|
| **1** | *Psycho* (1960) – Alfred Hitchcock | Psychological thriller | Iconic shower scene; masterful use of suspense over gore. |
| **2** | *Halloween* (1978) – John Carpenter | Slasher | Introduced Michael Myers; minimalist score creates relentless tension. |
| **3** | *The Shining* (1980) – Stanley Kubrick | Gothic/psychological | Ambiguous reality vs madness; unforgettable imagery. |
| **4** | *A Nightmare on Elm Street* (1984) – Wes Craven | Supernatural slasher | Freddy Krueger blends dream logic with visceral fear. |
| **5** | *Candyman* (1992) – Bernard Rose | Urban folklore | Combines myth with social critique; haunting visual style. |
| **6** | *Scream* (1996) – Wes Craven | Meta‑slasher | Self‑aware humor meets genuine scares; revitalized the genre. |
| **7** | *28 Days Later* (2002) – Danny Boyle | Post‑apocalyptic infection | Fast‑moving zombies + emotional core; redefined “zombie” pacing. |
| **8** | *Paranormal Activity* (2007) – Oren Peli | Found footage / hauntings | Low budget but high impact through realistic camera work. |
| **9** | *Hereditary* (2018) – Ari Aster | Family trauma + occult | Intense atmosphere, unsettling performances, and a chilling finale. |
| **10** | *Midsommar* (2019) – Ari Aster | Folk horror | Daylight dread; ritualistic violence set against pastoral beauty. |
| **11** | *Get Out* (2017) – Jordan Peele | Horror‑comedy/social satire | Sharp commentary wrapped in a tense thriller package. |
| **12** | *It Follows* (2014) – David Robert Mitchell | Modern urban legend | Creepy premise (“you’ll never escape”) delivered via steady dread. |
| **13** | *The Babadook* (2014) – Jennifer Kent | Psychological monster | Uses motherhood anxiety as metaphor for a literal beast. |
| **14** | *Us* (2019) – Jordan Peele | Duality / body horror | Mirror image concept turned terrifyingly personal. |
| **15** | *Evil Dead II* (1987) – Sam Raimi | Campy splatter | Over-the-top gore combined with clever comedy. |

### Quick Streaming Guide (as of mid‑2026)

| Movie | Where You Can Watch |
|-------|---------------------|
| Psycho | Amazon Prime Video |
| Halloween | Netflix (US), Hulu (UK) |
| The Shining | HBO Max |
| A Nightmare on Elm Street | Peacock |
| Candyman | Paramount+ |
| Scream | Disney+ (in select regions) |
| 28 Days Later | Apple TV+ |
| Paranormal Activity | Hulu |
| Hereditary | Netflix |
| Midsommar | HBO Max |
| Get Out | Amazon Prime Video |
| It Follows | Hulu |
| The Babadook | Amazon Prime Video |
| Us | HBO Max |
| Evil Dead II | Tubi (free ad-supported) |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want chills from a haunted house, existential dread, or just a good old-fashioned scream fest! Enjoy the fright night.
